atoms.canonical_statement: The trial aimed to assess the clinical validity of circulating tumour DNA testing and the clinical utility of using ctDNA results to select mutation-directed therapy in advanced breast cancer.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We aimed to assess the clinical validity of ctDNA testing, and to investigate the clinical utility of using ctDNA to select targeted therapies for patients without previous tissue testing.

atoms.canonical_statement: plasmaMATCH was a multicohort, open-label, non-randomised, phase 2a clinical trial platform conducted across 18 UK hospitals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: plasmaMATCH is a multicohort, open-label, non-randomised, phase 2a clinical trial platform run across 18 UK hospitals

atoms.canonical_statement: The registered study population comprised women with advanced breast cancer who entered ctDNA screening or, for seven cohort D participants, entered through previous tumour sequencing.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Between Dec 21, 2016, and April 26, 2019, 1051 patients were registered into the study (1044 via ctDNA screening, seven via previous tumour sequencing; figure 1; appendix p 17)

population.label: Registered plasmaMATCH population

atoms.canonical_statement: Key registration criteria included age at least 18 years, histologically confirmed advanced breast cancer not suitable for curative treatment, measurable disease, ECOG performance status 0 to 2, life expectancy over 3 months, and prior treatment for advanced disease or relapse within 12 months of neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Eligible patients were women at least 18 years of age with histologically confirmed advanced breast cancer that was not suitable for treatment with radical or curative intent, who had measurable disease, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0–2, estimated life expectancy of more than 3 months

population.label: Registration-eligible women with advanced breast cancer
inclusion_criteria: Histologically confirmed advanced breast cancer not suitable for curative intent

atoms.canonical_statement: Registration excluded uncontrolled CNS or cardiac disease, ongoing grade 1 or higher toxicity from previous treatment, and other malignancy within the previous 3 years, with additional cohort-specific criteria.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Exclusion criteria for ctDNA testing included uncontrolled CNS or cardiac disease, ongoing toxicities of grade 1 or higher from previous treatments, and malignancies of other types within the past 3 years.

population.label: Registration candidates
exclusion_criteria: Ongoing toxicity grade >=1 from previous treatment

atoms.canonical_statement: A positive result from either ctDNA assay was sufficient for treatment cohort entry, and mutations qualifying for cohorts B to D took precedence over cohort A when more than one target mutation was found.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A positive result by either ctDNA assay was sufficient for cohort entry. If more than one mutation was identified, entry to cohorts B–D took preference to cohort A.

atoms.canonical_statement: Cohort A treated ctDNA ESR1-mutant disease with extended-dose fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly on days 1, 8, and 15 of cycle 1 and days 1 and 15 from cycle 2 onward.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cohort A included individuals with ESR1 mutations; they received extended-dose 500 mg fulvestrant administered intramuscularly on days 1, 8, and 15 in cycle 1, and days 1 and 15 in cycle 2 onwards, on a 28-day cycle.

exposures.frequency: days 1, 8, and 15 in cycle 1; days 1 and 15 from cycle 2 onward

atoms.canonical_statement: Cohort B treated HER2-mutant disease with neratinib 240 mg orally once daily, adding standard-dose fulvestrant for oestrogen receptor-positive disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cohort B included individuals with HER2 mutations; they received 240 mg neratinib orally once a day on a continuous schedule. In patients with oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, this treatment was administered together with fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly at standard dosing

exposures.frequency: once daily
days 1 and 15 in cycle 1; day 1 from cycle 2 onward

atoms.canonical_statement: Cohort C treated AKT1-mutant, oestrogen receptor-positive disease with capivasertib 400 mg twice daily on a 4-days-on, 3-days-off schedule plus standard-dose fulvestrant.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cohort C included individuals with AKT1 mutations and oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer; they received 400 mg capivasertib orally twice a day for 4 days on followed by 3 days off continuously with fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly at standard dosing.

exposures.frequency: twice daily for 4 days on, 3 days off
days 1 and 15 in cycle 1; day 1 from cycle 2 onward

atoms.canonical_statement: Cohort D treated AKT1-mutant oestrogen receptor-negative disease or PTEN-altered disease with capivasertib 480 mg monotherapy twice daily on a 4-days-on, 3-days-off schedule.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This cohort received 480 mg capivasertib monotherapy orally, twice a day for 4 days on, followed by 3 days off, continuously.

exposures.frequency: twice daily for 4 days on, 3 days off

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary endpoint for cohorts A to D was confirmed objective response rate, defined as a confirmed complete or partial response by RECIST version 1.1 during trial treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary endpoint for cohorts A–D was confirmed objective response rate defined as a confirmed complete response or partial response according to RECIST criteria at any point during trial treatment.

outcome.definition: Confirmed complete response or partial response according to RECIST version 1.1 during trial treatment

atoms.canonical_statement: Clinical benefit was defined as complete response, partial response, or stable disease lasting more than 6 months during trial treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: clinical benefit rate (defined as complete response, partial response, or stable disease for more than 6 months during trial treatment)

outcome.definition: Complete response, partial response, or stable disease for more than 6 months during trial treatment

atoms.canonical_statement: Progression-free survival was defined from cohort entry to confirmed RECIST progression or death from any cause.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: progression-free survival (defined as time from cohort entry to first date of either confirmed progression of disease according to RECIST criteria or death from any cause)

outcome.definition: Time from cohort entry to confirmed RECIST progression or death from any cause

atoms.canonical_statement: CT or MRI and bone imaging were performed at baseline; CT or MRI was repeated every 8 weeks through week 32 and every 12 weeks thereafter, without independent central review of disease outcome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients underwent CT or MRI scan and bone scan at baseline, with CT or MRI scan repeated every 8 weeks until 32 weeks after commencing treatment, and every 12 weeks thereafter, for disease evaluation using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1 criteria. There was no independent central review of disease outcome.

atoms.canonical_statement: All four cohorts used a single-stage A’Hern design with one-sided alpha 5% and 80% power; cohort A required at least 13 responses among 78 evaluable patients to infer activity, while cohorts B, C, and D required at least 3 responses among 16 evaluable patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All cohorts used a single-stage A’Hern design with α 5%, to have 80% power.

atoms.canonical_statement: Digital PCR was performed centrally for hotspot mutations in PIK3CA, ESR1, HER2, and AKT1; prospective Guardant360 targeted sequencing was added from July 10, 2018.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Digital droplet PCR was done at a central laboratory ... prospectively in all patients, for mutations in PIK3CA, ESR1, HER2, and AKT1. From July 10, 2018 ... prospective testing also included error-corrected targeted sequencing with Guardant360

exposures.details: Central digital PCR testing for hotspot mutations

atoms.canonical_statement: The supplementary digital PCR protocol required at least 10,000 droplets per well, at least 2 mutant FAM-positive droplets, more than 300 wild-type VIC droplets, and repeat confirmation in a separate assay.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: dPCR assays were considered positive when there were a minimum of 10,000 total droplets per well, with two or more positive FAM droplets (mutant), and >300 VIC droplets (wild type). Each positive result was repeated in a separate assay, with a second positive result required for validation.

atoms.canonical_statement: The supplement defined clonally dominant ESR1 mutations as a cancer fraction of at least 50% and subclonal ESR1 mutations as a cancer fraction below 50%, using allele fraction relative to the maximum allele fraction in the sample.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: ESR1 mutations with a cancer fraction >=50% were termed clonally dominant and with cancer fraction <50% were termed subclonal.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that ctDNA testing offered accurate and rapid genotyping with sufficient clinical validity to select mutation-directed therapy in advanced breast cancer.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: ctDNA testing offers accurate, rapid genotyping that enables the selection of mutation-directed therapies for patients with breast cancer, with sufficient clinical validity for adoption into routine clinical practice.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that HER2 and AKT1 mutations identified by ctDNA were clinically targetable based on the activity observed with neratinib and capivasertib-based therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our results demonstrate clinically relevant activity of targeted therapies against rare HER2 and AKT1 mutations, confirming these mutations could be targetable for breast cancer treatment.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors identified heavy prior treatment as a possible reason for lower targeted-drug activity, especially in cohort A.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our study has limitations. Inclusion of relatively heavily pretreated patients might reduce activity of the targeted drugs, especially in cohort A

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial did not target PIK3CA mutations, so only 17 of 1051 registered patients, or 1.6%, had a response to therapy across the study.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The study was designed to assess the activity of therapies against specific genomic events, but it did not target PIK3CA mutations, and as a result relatively few of the patients registered to the trial had a response to therapy (17 [1·6%] of 1051 patients).

atoms.canonical_statement: Disease response was investigator assessed without independent central review.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There was no independent central review of disease outcome.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors stated that tissue biopsy remained important for immunohistochemistry and copy-number assessment despite the strong ctDNA results.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: However, we note that tissue biopsy will remain important for immunohistochemistry, and for copy number-based assessment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: NCT, AR, JMB, LSK, CS, LM, SK, KW, SM, HB, MH, BK, and RC report grants from Cancer Research UK, grants and non-financial support in the form of study drug provision from AstraZeneca and Puma Biotechnology, non-financial support in the form of ctDNA sequencing from Guardant Health, and provision of reagents from BioRad, during the conduct of the study.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors stated that de-identified individual participant data and a data dictionary would be available to researchers on request after formal data-access approval under ICR-CTSU policy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: De-identified individual participant data, together with a data dictionary defining each field in the dataset, will be made available to other researchers on request, subject to approval of a formal data access request in accordance with the ICR-CTSU data and sample access policy.
